column1: # Third-party code inside FEX's source tree that the engine's FEX builds compile, and the licenses/ file that
# carries its notice. tools/fex-notices.py (package.sh runs it) lists every file the FEX builds read
# (`ninja -t deps` of work/build/fex-*) below FEX's tree and stops the packaging if one has a copyright line,
# a public-domain statement or an SPDX licence other than FEX's own MIT and no line here covers it, or if a
# licenses/ file named here is missing. "-" means no notice is needed; the last column says why.
# Format (tab separated): path pattern (fnmatch, relative to FEX's tree)  licenses/ files (comma separated) or -  what it is

column3: Berkeley SoftFloat 3e, BSD-3-Clause (the notice is the leading comment of its source files)
functions taken from VIXL (Copyright 2015, VIXL authors), BSD-3-Clause; the notice is the file's own leading comment. The VIXL library itself (External/vixl) is not compiled

musl libc routines in FEX's Windows runtime (Rich Felker et al.; exp2 and log2 by Arm Limited), MIT; the files carry only SPDX lines, so the text is musl's own COPYRIGHT file, from Wine's copy of musl
mingw-w64's load-config stub, which says it is placed in the public domain
FEX's own file (MIT); its SplitMix64 fallback is Sebastiano Vigna's public-domain (CC0) reference code
